The casting was announced on Monday, November 16, 2026, by Amazon MGM Studios and the official James Bond social media account, ending months of speculation over who would take over the role. A post on the 007 account confirmed the decision with the message, “Identity Confirmed,” alongside a short video featuring Pattinson and the words, “James Bond will return.” The 40-year-old actor becomes the latest in a line of performers to portray the fictional British secret agent, following Craig, who played Bond in five films from Casino Royale (2006) to No Time to Die (2021). Pattinson is widely recognised for his role as Edward Cullen in the Twilight film series and as Bruce Wayne in The Batman. His other credits include Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Tenet and The Lighthouse. The upcoming 26th Bond film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, known for the Dune franchise, while Steven Knight, creator of Peaky Blinders, is writing the screenplay. Producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman are overseeing the project, which marks the first Bond film under Amazon MGM Studios’ creative control following its agreement with the franchise’s previous rights holders. Pattinson previously worked with Villeneuve on the upcoming film Dune: Part Three. The title and release date of the new James Bond film have not yet been announced.
